title: IMMUNE DYSREGULATION WITH AUTOIMMUNITY, AUTOINFLAMMATION, AND IMMUNODEFICIENCY

intro.text: This entry describes immune dysregulation with autoimmunity, autoinflammation, and immunodeficiency (IDAAI). Variants in the IRAK2 gene were reported by Amali et al. (2024) in patients with severe invasive infections.

checks.claim: Amali et al. (2024) reported variants in the IRAK2 gene in patients with severe invasive infections.
checks.evidence_quote: In two patients with sequential or repeated invasive infections: herpes simplex virus-triggered hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia with candidemia respectively, novel mutations of IRAK2 were identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports IRAK2 mutations in patients with invasive infections.

paragraphs.text: Amali et al. (2024) described 2 patients who had invasive infections one after another or repeatedly. One patient had hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis triggered by herpes simplex virus, together with tuberculosis. The other patient had Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia and candidemia.

paragraphs.text: Amali et al. (2024) identified new variants in the IRAK2 gene in 2 patients with severe invasive infections. The variants impaired IRAK2's ability to ubiquitinate the signal adaptor TRAF6 and reduced TNF-alpha production. The authors suggested that IRAK2 may play a central role in host defense against infection.

checks.explanation: The abstract reports novel IRAK2 mutations in two patients.

checks.claim: The IRAK2 variants identified by Amali et al. (2024) impaired IRAK2's ability to ubiquitinate the signal adaptor TRAF6.
checks.evidence_quote: These mutations compromised the capacity to ubiquinate (or functionally modify) the signal adaptor tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutations compromised the capacity to ubiquitinate TRAF6, which matches the claim.

checks.claim: Amali et al. (2024) suggested that IRAK2 may play a central role in host defense against infection.
checks.evidence_quote: This susceptibility to a varied range of pathogens underlines a potential central role played by IRAK2 in mediating host defense in infectious diseases.
checks.explanation: The abstract proposes a potential central role for IRAK2 in host defense.
